rendered:
According to the US Advanced Battery Consortium standards, the review says an EV battery reaches the end of its usable life when its current cell capacity falls below the rated capacity threshold: "an EV battery reaches the end of its usable life when its current[1] "cell capacity is less than 80% of the rated capacity[2]".

What can be done with such batteries: the review states that end-of-life EV batteries "can be reused/repurposed, recycled, or[3] disposed in landfills, which it notes would cause serious environmental issues. Reuse takes the form of repurposing, where the batteries are reconfigured for a second life in applications such as grid energy storage and behind-the-meter energy storage.

Which of these the review says they all eventually need: regardless of whether the batteries are reused, "they will eventually need to be[4] recycled[5]. So recycling is the outcome the review identifies as unavoidable for all such batteries.
